decided: A broken Jira site does not count toward the stage or the jira step; only `jira.connected > 0` counts and `jira.broken` is never read, so a workspace with only broken sites is `"barebone"`.
Ticket: silent.
Instead: Treat a broken site as connected for staging, or add a separate stage or flag that prompts reconnection.
A GitHub account with linked installations but no repository picked counts as the github stage: `github.repositories > 0 || github.connected > 0`.
Ticket: silent.
Instead: Require at least one repository for the github stage, so an account alone stays barebone.
The stage ignores `available`; it uses only the connected and repository counts.
Ticket: silent.
Instead: Treat an unavailable tool as not connected, whatever its counts say.
The github step is done only when `github.repositories > 0`; a connected account with no repository leaves it not done.
Ticket: silent.
Instead: Mark it done once `github.connected > 0`, matching the stage logic.
The size step is done when `proposals > 0`; bounties are not counted.
Ticket: silent.
Instead: Count bounties too, or count either proposals or bounties.
Steps are listed github, size, jira in the github stage, and jira, github, size in every other stage.
Ticket: silent.
Instead: Use one fixed order (jira, github, size) for every stage.
When the server does not offer Jira or GitHub, that tool's step is dropped and the remaining steps are still returned.
Ticket: silent.
Instead: Keep the step and mark it done or disabled, or return an empty list.
When every listed step is done, no step is current (all have `current: false`).
Ticket: silent.
Instead: Leave the last step marked current, or return no steps.
The current step is the first not-done step in the listed order; a later step can be done while an earlier one stays current.
Ticket: silent.
Instead: Mark the next step after the last completed one as current.
`setupComplete` is `every` step done over the listed steps, so it depends on availability: with both tools unavailable it is decided by the size step alone (and would be true for an empty list).
Ticket: silent.
Instead: Require at least one step to be done, or ignore tool availability when judging completion.
`canManage`, `jira.boards` and `bounties` affect neither the stage, nor the steps, nor completion.
Ticket: silent.
Instead: Require boards for the jira stage, or hide steps from users who cannot manage.
The jira step is done when `jira.connected > 0`, the same test the stage uses; boards are not required.
Ticket: silent.
Instead: Mark the jira step done only once the site has at least one board (`jira.boards > 0`).
A count is present only when it is `> 0`: negative and `NaN` counts are treated as absent, fractions above zero as present, and no function throws or validates.
Ticket: silent.
Instead: Reject non-integer or negative counts with a `RangeError`.
`setupComplete` reports only whether the checklist is done; whether a person has hidden it is not a fact here and is decided by the caller.
Ticket: "A getting-started checklist sits above every stage until it is done or hidden."
Instead: Add a `hidden` field to `SetupFacts` and have `setupComplete` (or `setupSteps` returning `[]`) account for it.
The functions are pure: they do not change their input (deeply frozen facts are accepted), and each `setupSteps` call returns a new array of new objects with exactly the keys `id`, `done`, `current`.
Ticket: silent.
Instead: Return shared, frozen step lists for each case, or let steps carry extra fields such as a label.
